title: centaurea rupestris subsp. finazzeri
intro: Centaurea rupestris subsp. finazzeri, commonly known as a rare species of mountain cornflower, is a flowering plant native to the Alps. It is traditionally used in herbal medicine to treat various health conditions due to its reported health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties that may help soothe digestive issues and alleviate respiratory problems. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its ability to reduce inflammation, promote wound healing, and exhibit antioxidant properties, which contribute to its potential use in treating skin conditions and oxidative stress-related disorders. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenes, which have been identified in studies as the primary compounds contributing to the plant's medicinal properties.
